players.product: photonic quantum systems built on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) chips

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 2026 revenue totaled $5.6 million, compared to $61,000 in Q2 2025 and $3.7 million in Q1 2026; all business units contributed, from a broad cross-section of government, educational and commercial customers, mainly from sales of photonics products.
quarterly_data.figure: $5.6 million Q2 2026 revenue (vs $61,000 Q2 2025; $3.7 million Q1 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 2026 operating expenses totaled $21.8 million versus $10.2 million in Q2 2025 (up 114%), largely from personnel costs for R&D and sales and marketing plus approximately $7.3 million of acquisition-related transaction expenses; interest and other income was $13 million (vs $1.8 million); net loss was $11.8 million, or $0.05 per share (vs $36.5 million), including a $1.7 million non-cash mark-to-market loss on the warrant derivative liability (vs $28 million in Q2 2025).
quarterly_data.figure: $21.8 million operating expenses; $11.8 million net loss

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled approximately $1.3 billion at June 30, 2026, compared to approximately $1.5 billion at year-end 2025, reflecting the acquisitions of Luminar Semiconductor, NuCrypt and NHanced Semiconductors; total assets approximately $1.6 billion, total liabilities $47.2 million.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$1.3 billion cash, cash equivalents and investments

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: contract backlog was approximately $42.5 million as of June 30, 2026; much of the increase from the end of Q1 relates to NHanced, plus business development wins across the company. The contracts are performed over 12-18 months; if nothing else came in, the backlog 'would keep us going until third quarter of next year, maybe a little bit longer'; there has not been a lot of change in the 40 days since quarter end.

CFO: QCi is still not giving formal guidance but stands by models showing QCi before NHanced doing $20 million-$25 million for this year; NHanced's contribution is estimated somewhere between the $7 million and $16 million it has done in the past (it did about $16 million in the first half of last year), depending on how quickly projects are delivered and accepted; Funding on a big U.S. Navy contract has been pushed to next year; he cautions modellers to 'err on the back-loading'.
quarterly_data.figure: $20 million-$25 million (QCi before NHanced, this year); NHanced between $7 million and $16 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: roughly 70%-80% of QCi's business comes from government contracting, mainly as a subcontractor to primes on the civil side and in aerospace and defense; commercial is second and educational a distant third. He expects that to continue for a while, with the balance gradually shifting toward commercial.

CEO: in April QCi announced that NeuraWave, its next-generation photonic reservoir computing platform combining photonic and digital computing for energy-efficient AI inference and signal processing at the edge, reached commercial readiness; target applications include defense, telecommunications, autonomous vehicles, robotics, healthcare and industrial monitoring.

Customer Planck Dynamics: CEO says QCi reached a framework agreement in June with Planck Dynamics that included an initial purchase order for five NeuraWave photonic reservoir computing systems; it provides a pathway for the potential deployment of multiple dozens of NeuraWave systems as customer milestones are achieved, 'representing a potential aggregate program value of more than $10 million'.
quarterly_data.figure: initial purchase order for five NeuraWave systems; potential aggregate program value of more than $10 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: in June QCi delivered and installed its Dirac-3 quantum optimization machine at a global consulting firm (not named), deployed to support the firm's engagements with its enterprise customers on complex optimization such as portfolio optimization. QCi also received a purchase order from a world-leading university (not named) for its quantum secure communications system, to be evaluated for quantum secure networking research.

CEO on Dirac-3 (a room-temperature photonic machine for NP-hard optimization, not a quantum annealer): QCi has made 'pretty good progress' on supporting more variables and more functionality — 'watch out for some news coming out in the coming months'; he says own engineers and outside users benchmarking it reported 'pretty clear advantage' over classical approaches and other quantum machines, and he believes at least a portion of the data has been published in journals.

CEO on the gate-based roadmap: 'we currently don't have gate-based machine yet, but we have been making very good progress' ('climbing the last half mile'); a room-temperature single-photon machine needs lasers, single photon detectors and control electronics integrated on a single chip, which he gives as the fundamental reason QCi acquired Luminar Semiconductor and NHanced — to develop heterogeneous integrated chips for quantum computing, sensing, communications and photonic AI.

CEO: QCi's technology and manufacturing capabilities 'have reached an inflection point' and it is ready to address the market at sizable scale; the CFO says QCi will emphasize sales, including key hires in commercial and government sales, to build backlog. For the second half of 2026 the CEO's focus is integrating the recent acquisitions and moving from prototyping toward scalable commercial manufacturing, while continuing to evaluate targeted acquisitions.

players.product: TFLN photonic chip foundry services (AZ Chips Facility, ASU Research Park, Tempe AZ)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: QCi completed the acquisition of NHanced Semiconductors in Q2, which it calls the leading independent U.S.-based advanced packaging foundry (hybrid bonding, chiplet architectures, silicon interposers, photonic device integration), launching its Fab 2 initiative ahead of schedule alongside Fab 1 in Tempe, Arizona; it adds customer base, production capacity and an engineering team and strengthens production for the TFLN platform. CFO: the NHanced facility 'can currently do roughly 60,000 wafers a year', a substantial increase over Fab 1.

CFO: QCi is planning upgrades to the NHanced (Fab 2) facility — less than building a whole new facility, 'probably in the $50 million-$100 million range. Probably closer to $75 million' — still in the planning stages, and 'we're probably not going to spend anywhere near that this year'.
quarterly_data.figure: $50 million-$100 million range, probably closer to $75 million (planned)
